text: Benchmark note. The existing Postgres-backed work queue stayed within the first-release latency and throughput targets under the realistic load profile. No Kafka comparison was required to establish this baseline.
title: Juniper queue baseline

author: workspace_user
text: We decided not to add Kafka for the first release because operating another stateful platform would add ownership and failure-mode complexity. This is not a claim that Kafka is technically poor. Reopen the decision only if realistic measurements show the current queue cannot meet the release requirement.
title: First-release queue decision

text: Performance note. A synthetic burst at about fifteen times the expected first-release load produced queue delay. The burst is intentionally unrealistic for current traffic. The next action is realistic measurement; this note does not record a reversal of the first-release queue decision.
title: Synthetic queue spike

text: INC-204 update at 10:02. API CPU is elevated and request latency is rising. Initial working hypothesis: a memory leak may be the cause. The hypothesis is unconfirmed.
title: INC-204 initial observation

text: INC-204 update at 10:17. Retry volume rose immediately after the client-timeout rollout. Disabling automatic retries caused API CPU and queue depth to fall. The team began rolling back the timeout change.
title: INC-204 retry signal

text: INC-204 postmortem. Root cause: the client-timeout rollout triggered retry amplification. Elevated CPU was a downstream symptom. Heap analysis found no memory leak, so the initial memory-leak hypothesis is rejected. The corrected incident start time is 10:02.
title: INC-204 postmortem

text: INC-204 addendum. An earlier circulated timeline listed 10:00 as the start. Source logs show the incident began at 10:02. Correct the start time only; the retry-amplification root-cause assessment remains unchanged.
title: INC-204 timing correction

text: Contract memo for customer Maple. Production customer data must remain in Canada. The same geographic restriction applies to backups and replicas. Encryption does not waive the geographic requirement.
title: Maple Canada residency rule

text: HelixCloud response. Primary storage can be located in Canada. Under the standard disaster-recovery configuration, encrypted backups may be stored in the United States. A Canada-only disaster-recovery option is available on the enterprise configuration, but it is not the default.
title: HelixCloud disaster-recovery options

text: Procurement meeting. Maple asked where disaster-recovery copies would be stored. HelixCloud could not confirm during the meeting that every copy in the standard configuration stays in Canada.
title: Maple procurement discussion
